meta.title: The Gladden Line
intro: This record starts with Olivia Gene Gladden and Evan Elliot Gladden, then their parents, Gene Gladden and Emily Gladden, and then walks back through the Gladden fathers as far as the papers go.
It was set down on 23 November 2026. No person, date, or kinship has been added beyond the research. If a link is unproven, the card says so before it is opened.
Olivia, Evan, Gene, and Emily are living, so they are shown by name only. Gene's birthplace, Groves, Texas, is the one place included for him.
The old records spell the name Gladden, Gladen, Gleden, gladding, and Gladiney. The spelling in each note is the spelling on that page.

The ground of the early records is Wateree Creek, in Fairfield County, South Carolina. Jesse Gladden is documented there. Reaching him from the later family depends on John, and that link is unproven. William and Richard are candidates. Earlier than that, the search continues.

line.title: William Silas Gladden
line.summary: The generation before William Noah. Born in South Carolina about 1826–1829. His wife was Nancy. On the census in Louisiana in 1870 and 1880.

people.name: William Silas Gladden
people.relation: The generation before William Noah Gladden. Born in South Carolina about 1826–1829.
paragraphs: William Silas Gladden is the generation before William Noah in this line. He was born in South Carolina about 1826–1829. His wife was Nancy, the Nancy of this Louisiana household.
The 1870 census lists him in Ouachita Parish, Louisiana, as "Wm Gladen," age 44, with a son Wm, age 10.
The 1880 census lists him in Alexandria, Louisiana, as "W. S. Gladden," age 51, with Nancy, Laura, Columbia, and John.
Laura, Columbia, and John are names in that 1880 household. These notes do not give them a kinship beyond that.

line.title: John Gladden
line.summary: About 1796–1849, of Fairfield County, married to Rebecca Coleman. Gene treats him as the father of William Silas. No record proves that link.

people.name: John Gladden
people.relation: Assumed father of William Silas Gladden. About 1796–1849, Fairfield County, South Carolina.
paragraphs: John Gladden, about 1796–1849, of Fairfield County, South Carolina, is the step this research uses between William Silas and Jesse. Gene chose to treat John as William Silas's father. No record proves it yet.
He married Rebecca Coleman. He sold land to Middleton Gladden in 1816, and to Silas Gladden in about 1836.
A compiled source says he married Nancy Hollis. These notes mark that claim unproven. Nancy, the daughter of Moses Hollis, is kept beside the line, because no record names her husband.
Jesse's 1821 will names a son John. These notes do not prove that the son in the will and this John, of about 1796–1849, are the same man.
sources: Working line chosen by Gene: John Gladden (about 1796–1849) of Fairfield County as the father of William Silas. No record proving the link is cited.
Married Rebecca Coleman, as carried in this research.
Sold land to Middleton Gladden in 1816, and to Silas Gladden in about 1836.
A compiled source says he married Nancy Hollis. Unproven.

line.title: Jesse Gladden
line.summary: Died 1821 in Fairfield County. His will names his wife Nelly. His own records are solid. The step to him through John is still unproven.

see.label: His 96 acres, plotted as an estimate

people.name: Jesse Gladden
paragraphs: Jesse Gladden died in 1821 in Fairfield County, South Carolina. His will of that year names his wife Nelly, and sons including Silas, born about 1790, William, born about 1795, and John. He signed by mark, and so could not write.
In 1786 he witnessed William Gladden's purchase of land on Nixon's Creek. The deed is Fairfield Deeds Book A, page 294. His mark is on that page.
In 1794 he bought a horse at the sale of the Moses Hollis estate, and signed the appraisers' oath as "Jassey Gleden."
On 19 February 1800 he bought 96 acres on a branch of Wateree Creek, bordered by John Barber. That deed is Book N, page 78. He sold the land to John Barber in 1814.
He served in the Revolutionary militia alongside William Gladden. The notes name no rank and no company.
The will's son John, and the John of about 1796–1849, are not proven to be the same man. This line reaches Jesse only by the choice Gene has made, which a record has not yet shown.
sources: Will dated 1821, Fairfield County, South Carolina. Names his wife Nelly and sons including Silas (born about 1790), William (born about 1795), and John. Signed by mark.
Fairfield Deeds Book A, page 294. 1786. Witnessed William Gladden's purchase on Nixon's Creek, and signed by mark.
Moses Hollis estate sale, 1794. Bought a horse, and signed the appraisers' oath as "Jassey Gleden."

line.title: Nancy (Hollis) Gladden
line.summary: Daughter of Moses Hollis. His will calls her "my Daughter Nancy gladding." No record names her husband, so she is not fixed as Jesse's wife or as John's.

see.label: Her 100 acres, plotted as an estimate

people.name: Nancy (Hollis) Gladden
people.relation: Daughter of Moses Hollis. Husband unnamed.
paragraphs: The will of Moses Hollis, written on 9 April 1793 and proved in 1794, names "my Daughter Nancy gladding."
In 1797 her brother Berry Hollis sold her 100 acres on a branch of Wateree Creek, and gave her an enslaved man named Tom, "for love and affection." The deed is Book L, page 90.
This research calls her a possible first wife of Jesse, or else a wife of John. Her husband is never named. Both possibilities stay open, and neither is treated as fact.
sources: Will of Moses Hollis, written 9 April 1793, proved 1794. Names "my Daughter Nancy gladding."
Deed Book L, page 90. 1797. Berry Hollis sold her 100 acres on a branch of Wateree Creek, and gave her an enslaved man named Tom, "for love and affection."
Her husband is not named in these records.

people.name: William Gladden
people.relation: Died 1793. Probable brother of Jesse, and his neighbor. The brotherhood is not proven.
paragraphs: William Gladden died in 1793. He and Jesse both lived on branches of Wateree Creek. Compilers call them brothers. No record proves it, so he stands beside the line rather than on it.
On 25 November 1770 he bought 150 acres on a branch of Wateree Creek, in St. Mark's Parish, from William Goen. The deed is Book G, page 35.
About 1783 he was an appraiser of the estate of James Land, in Camden District.
In 1786 he bought 100 acres on Nixon's Creek, next to John Barber. Jesse witnessed that deed.
He served in the Revolutionary militia alongside Jesse. The notes name no rank and no company.
His wife, Elizabeth Gladden, died in 1858 at the age of 107, and is buried at Gladden-Powell Cemetery.

His son Minor Gladden (1787–1867) was the father of Confederate Gen. Adley Hogan Gladden (1810–1862). Minor and Adley are recorded with this William. They are not steps on the line back through Jesse.
sources: Deed Book G, page 35. 25 November 1770. Bought 150 acres on a branch of Wateree Creek, in St. Mark's Parish, from William Goen.
About 1783, appraiser of the James Land estate, Camden District.
1786. Bought 100 acres on Nixon's Creek, next to John Barber. Jesse witnessed the deed (Fairfield Deeds Book A, page 294).
This research: served in the Revolutionary militia alongside Jesse. No rank or company is named.
Wife Elizabeth Gladden died in 1858 at age 107, buried at Gladden-Powell Cemetery.
Son Minor Gladden (1787–1867), father of Confederate Gen. Adley Hogan Gladden (1810–1862).
Compilers call him a brother of Jesse. No record cited here proves the brotherhood.

line.title: Richard Gladen
line.summary: Died about 1782–1783. His widow was Ann. He is old enough to be the father of William and of Jesse, and no record says that he was.

people.name: Richard Gladen
people.relation: Died about 1782–1783. A candidate for the father of William and Jesse. Not proven.
paragraphs: Richard Gladen died about 1782–1783. Ann was his widow. He is the right age to be the father of the William who died in 1793 and of Jesse. No record says that he was, so he remains a candidate.
On 16 October 1775 he witnessed the will of John Phillips of Jacksons Creek. The record writes his name "Richard Gladiney." The will is Camden Estate Book A-1, page 75.

On 17 December 1783 his estate was appraised at £146.17.10½. The appraisement is Camden Book A-1, page 130. His widow, Ann, was the main buyer at the sale, and among her purchases was an enslaved man, for £42.
About 1789, "Ann Gladden, widow," bought 100 acres on Mill Branch of Wateree Creek. By 1814 she was living in Putnam County, Georgia, and she sold that land.
sources: Camden Estate Book A-1, page 75. 16 October 1775. Witnessed the will of John Phillips of Jacksons Creek, as "Richard Gladiney."

searching.title: Still searching
searching.lede: The search continues. What follows are leads, not people added to this line, and not facts of kinship.

sections.title: Fairfax County, Virginia, a lead, probably not this line
paragraphs: William Gladdin is on record in Fairfax County, Virginia, from 1749 to March 1772. John, Catharine, and Frances Gladen are there from 1753 to 1762.
The William of the Wateree Creek deeds was already in South Carolina by 1770, so the Fairfax William is probably a different man. He is kept here as a lead. He is not added to the line.

sections.title: The 1600s
paragraphs: No record of this family has been found in the 1600s. That silence is not a finding about who the family was. It is the part of the search still open.

placesIntro: These places are in Fairfield County, South Carolina, in the country of Wateree Creek. A parcel pin is an estimate. The deeds do not give a modern survey, and the circle on the aerial map is only a guide. The cemeteries and Gladden Grove are plotted from the coordinates in the notes.
